Q: "Your Requirements could not be resolved to an installable set of packages" A:

In your php.ini file, you need to uncomment a line.
Replace ;extension=fileinfo withextension=fileinfo.

A hint is in the second line under Problem 1 of the error message :
[…] ext-fileinfo […] is missing from your system.
Install or enable PHP's fileinfo extension.

To find the location of php.ini, run php --ini.

Delete the project directory and create it again, either with the command you used –
composer create-project laravel/laravel <project-name> – or laravel new my-project.

Have you uncommented extension=fileinfo in php.ini and it still doesn't work?
You might need to grant administrator permissions to save your php.ini file.

To grant these permissions on Windows 10, do as follows.

  1. For me, it's C:/xampp/php/php.ini.
    In your case - C:\MAMP\bin\php\php7.4.1\php.ini

  2. Right-click on the file and click on properties.

  3. Security.

  4. Click on the Edit button.

  5. Click on each of the Group or user names and at the bottom where it says Permissions for authenticated Users, check Full control.

This way permission is granted, and now you should be able to save changes to the file.

Q: Why Bits declare instruction in nasm x86 assembly languages have no effect When I write code to similar bigmode in Bios? A:

but when it continue, the CPU should switch to real mode, but I found it still running 32 bits code, which cause the error

Indeed it is. Interestingly, it does switch to real mode yet it still runs 32-bit code. Relevant logs:

00014103085i[CPU0  ] CPU is in real mode (active)
00014103085i[CPU0  ] CS.mode = 32 bit
00014103085i[CPU0  ] | SEG sltr(index|ti|rpl)     base    limit G D
00014103085i[CPU0  ] |  CS:0000( 0001| 0|  0) 00000000 ffffffff 1 1

So this is why - CS descriptor cache still holds D=1 (which is the thing that determines whether 16-bit or 32-bit mode is active). Unreal mode works due to the fact limit stays the same as it was set before entering real mode and never gets overwritten whenever segment registers are reload. Things is, limit is not the only thing that is preserved in real mode. Everything but base gets preserved, and that includes DB flag. This is why any code that performs switching from 32-bit protected mode to 16-bit real mode must go through 16-bit PM to do so.

So you need to make sure your code in running in 16-bit PM mode before returning to the (un)real mode. Either add another 16-bit CS selector, or just forego 32-bit completely (you don't need it after all, you just need to drop to PM for a bit to reload descriptor caches and that can be done in 16 bit).

It is quite strange. I have added [BITS 16] in line 100. Why it still executing in 32 bits code?

Because this is not a CPU command, its an assembler directive. It does not switch CPU mode! Your program controls CPU and its modes, and BITS tells the assembler which particular part of the program is supposed to run in which mode (so it can emit machine code CPU could then understand). It is up to you to make sure directives that describe purported CPU mode and actual runtime CPU mode always match.
